sections.heading: Founder & Director
body: I started iFranchise with a simple belief: every entrepreneur deserves a fair shot at building something extraordinary. Too many brilliant business ideas die not from lack of potential, but from lack of the right guidance, capital, and strategic support.

We're not just connecting brands with investors - we're building dreams into empires. Every franchise we validate, every partnership we forge, and every expansion we architect is driven by one mission: turning your vision into a legacy that outlasts us all.
Your success is our legacy. Let's build something India will remember.
sections.name: Syed Abdul Khader

sections.heading: Co-Founder
body: I've spent over a decade watching businesses fail not because their ideas weren't good enough, but because they lacked the operational backbone to scale. That's what drives me every single day at iFranchise.

Scaling isn't just about opening more locations. It's about building systems so strong that your brand can thrive in 100 cities without losing its soul. It's about creating frameworks that turn chaos into clarity, and ambition into achievement.

We don't just advise - we roll up our sleeves and build alongside you. From market validation to operational excellence, we're in the trenches with every partner, ensuring no detail is overlooked and no opportunity is wasted.
Your growth is our obsession. Let's turn your brand into an unstoppable force.

faqs.question: How do I franchise my business?
faqs.answer: Start by checking whether another operator could deliver your business consistently. We help you review outlet economics, document operations, define your franchise model and prepare partner information. From there, we can plan how you’ll recruit, train and support franchise partners.

faqs.question: How much does franchise development cost?
faqs.answer: Your costs depend on the work you need: model development, operating manuals, training, investor information and professional documentation. Tell us what you’ve already prepared, and we’ll discuss a scope and fee proposal with you before work begins.

faqs.question: How do I find franchise investors?
faqs.answer: Begin with a clear partner profile and an offer that explains the investment, responsibilities and support. We can help you present your opportunity and organise investor conversations. Assess each potential partner against your requirements and give them room to review your business too.

faqs.question: How can I promote my franchise opportunity?
faqs.answer: Give prospective partners useful information about your business, costs, operating model and support. We can help you prepare a clear brand profile and discuss your outreach plan. Visibility is a starting point; relevant enquiries and thoughtful follow-up matter more than exposure alone.

faqs.question: Can I list my brand on iFranchise?
faqs.answer: Talk to us about your operating business, proposed franchise model and expansion plans. We’ll review the information you can provide and discuss the preparation and scope for a listing. Online intake is paused in this preview, so you can contact us by phone, email or WhatsApp.

faqs.question: What industries can be franchised?
faqs.answer: Franchising can be used in many industries, but your business needs repeatable operations, a workable commercial model and support for partners. Tell us how your business operates and where you want to expand, and we’ll discuss the preparation it may need.

faqs.question: What is included in a premium listing?
faqs.answer: We’ll agree the listing scope with you before work begins. It may cover your business profile, photographs, proposed investment, operating requirements and enquiry options. Ask us to explain the deliverables and any consulting or outreach support separately.

title: Frequently asked questions
intro: Find answers to your questions about investing in a franchise, expanding your brand and working with us.

faqs.question: What is iFranchise?
faqs.answer: We’re a franchise consulting company working with investors and business owners across India. We help you compare franchise opportunities, prepare your business for franchising and plan how you’ll expand.

faqs.question: How does iFranchise help franchise investors?
faqs.answer: You can explore brands by investment range, industry and operating model, then review the details of each opportunity. We help you prepare questions, understand the proposed responsibilities and organise discussions with the brand.

faqs.question: How does iFranchise help brand owners?
faqs.answer: We work with you to assess readiness, develop your franchise model, prepare partner information and plan expansion. You can also discuss a brand listing and the support you need for investor conversations and partner onboarding.

faqs.question: What franchise consulting services does iFranchise offer?
faqs.answer: We help you with franchise selection, model development, operating documentation, brand presentation, investor conversations, territory planning and partner preparation. We’ll agree the scope around your business and the work you need.

faqs.question: Does iFranchise work with first-time franchise investors?
faqs.answer: Yes. If this is your first business, we’ll help you compare models and understand the questions to ask about costs, operations, training and support. You’ll still need to assess your own readiness and review the proposal before you decide.

faqs.question: Can iFranchise help my brand become franchise-ready?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can work with you on your model, operating documentation, training requirements and investor information. We’ll identify what you’ve already prepared and what needs work before you recruit franchise partners.

faqs.question: Which industries does iFranchise cover?
faqs.answer: You can explore opportunities in food and beverage, retail, fashion and other sectors in our catalogue. If you’re developing a franchise in another industry, talk to us about your business and the support you need.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to start a franchise?
faqs.answer: Your total investment depends on the brand, format, property and location. Look beyond the franchise fee: ask for setup costs, deposits, stock, taxes, ongoing charges and working capital. Use the catalogue figures as starting points and request a current cost sheet before you decide.

faqs.question: What's the difference between FOCO, FOFO & FICO?
faqs.answer: These labels describe ownership, investment and operating responsibilities. FOFO commonly means franchise-owned, franchise-operated; FOCO means franchise-owned, company-operated; and FICO means franchise-invested, company-operated. Ask the brand to define exactly what you own, fund and manage in its agreement.

faqs.question: Is franchise business profitable in India?
faqs.answer: A franchise does not guarantee a profit. Your results depend on sales, costs, location, operations and the terms you agree. Ask for evidence behind financial projections and test how the business would perform if sales were lower or costs higher than expected.

faqs.question: What legal documents are required?
faqs.answer: Ask for the current franchise proposal, agreement and relevant operating and brand-use documents. The registrations and permissions you need depend on the activity and location. Have qualified advisers review your documents and confirm the applicable requirements before you commit.

faqs.question: How long does it take to launch a franchise?
faqs.answer: Your launch timeline depends on site selection, approvals, fit-out, staffing, training and the brand’s preparation. Ask for a plan with responsibilities and dependencies, then agree a realistic opening date once the key requirements are clear.

faqs.question: What is the typical investment range?
faqs.answer: Use the investment filter to explore the current catalogue, then check the full project cost for the format you’re considering. If you haven’t fixed a budget, tell us what you can invest and the working capital you want to keep available.

faqs.question: How long does it take to break even?
faqs.answer: There is no single timeline you can apply to every franchise. Review fixed costs, contribution margins, sales assumptions and cash requirements for your proposed outlet. Ask the brand to show how its projection changes under different scenarios.

faqs.question: Do I need prior business experience?
faqs.answer: Requirements vary by brand and operating model. Be clear about your experience, available time and the responsibilities you’re willing to take on. We can help you prepare questions about training, staffing and the support you would need.

faqs.question: What support does iFranchise provide?
faqs.answer: We help you compare opportunities, organise the commercial and operating questions, and prepare for discussions with brands. We’ll agree the scope with you so you know what support is included and what needs independent professional advice.

faqs.question: Can I operate multiple franchise units?
faqs.answer: You can discuss multi-unit opportunities with a brand, but the rights and conditions depend on its proposal. Review your staffing, funding and support capacity before committing to more locations, and make sure any development obligations are clear.

faqs.question: What does growth look like here?

title: Privacy Notice

sections.heading: Status of this notice
body: REQUIRES LEGAL REVIEW. This notice is a technical draft based on processing visible in the website code. It is not a legal certification. The registered legal entity operating under the iFranchise name, the applicable processing grounds, retention schedule, grievance contact, processor contracts, cross-border processing details, and the commencement of applicable DPDP Act and Rules provisions require confirmation.

sections.heading: Where this notice applies
body: This notice describes personal-data handling visible on the iFranchise website when a person submits an enquiry, requests a franchise brochure, expresses interest in a franchise, applies to list a brand, applies for a role, requests data-principal assistance, or chooses to use analytics preferences and external contact links.

sections.heading: Personal data collected
body: Depending on the form, the website may collect a name, email address, telephone number, company or brand details, state, city, preferred location, franchise or investment interests, enquiry message, job role, resume link, portfolio link, and request details. The form pipeline also attaches the source page, page URL, path, referrer, and submission timestamp. The website does not currently provide user accounts, collect passwords, accept direct resume uploads, or implement a payment-card form.

sections.heading: Purposes visible in the implementation
body: The collected information is used to receive and respond to contact and advisory enquiries, evaluate brand applications, handle interest in a named franchise, provide requested brochures, evaluate job applications, receive data-rights requests, prevent basic form abuse, operate the website, and measure website and form performance when analytics is permitted. Any additional use, including promotional email, SMS, telephone or WhatsApp marketing, requires business and legal confirmation and an appropriate separate choice where required.

sections.heading: How form data is handled
body: Submitted form information is validated and sanitised in the browser and sent over HTTPS to a Google Apps Script endpoint that appends it to a form-specific Google Sheets tab. When lead notifications are enabled in the deployment configuration, a Vercel serverless endpoint and Resend may also process a copy for an internal notification email. Google Sheet ownership, authorised users, email recipients, access-review procedures, backup practices, and storage regions are not established by this code and require business confirmation.

sections.heading: Franchise enquiries and other recipients
body: A franchise enquiry identifies the franchise in which the person expressed interest. The code stores that context with the enquiry. Whether identifiable enquiry data is subsequently shared with the relevant franchise brand, and under what controls, is an operational fact requiring business and legal confirmation. The code also contains user-initiated links to WhatsApp/Meta, Cal.com, Google Maps, telephone, email and social-sharing services; information entered after leaving the website is handled under the selected service’s own terms and privacy practices.

sections.heading: Analytics, cookies and device storage
body: The website uses first-party local or session storage for theme preference, scroll restoration, knowledge-hub progress, and the analytics-consent choice. Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics are intended to receive page and conversion events only after analytics consent. The exact tags in the live GTM container, GA4 settings, cookie names, retention settings, advertising features, and any additional pixels require a live configuration review. Analytics consent can be changed using the “Privacy choices” control in the website footer.

sections.heading: Retention
body: REQUIRES LEGAL REVIEW. The code does not define or enforce a retention period for Google Sheets rows, internal notification emails, data-rights requests, analytics data, or third-party services. No automated deletion or anonymisation job exists. The business must approve a purpose-specific retention schedule and operational deletion procedure before a definite period can be stated here.

sections.heading: Security controls and limitations
body: The implementation uses HTTPS endpoint validation, client-side field validation, payload sanitisation, honeypot fields, size limits, duplicate in-flight submission controls, and selected HTTP security headers. Access controls for Google Sheets and vendor systems are operational rather than defined in this repository. No internet service can be represented as completely secure, and this draft does not claim that security assessments, encryption at rest, or processor controls have been independently verified.

sections.heading: Data-principal requests
body: REQUIRES LEGAL REVIEW. Subject to applicable and commenced law, a person may request information about processing, access-related information, correction, completion or updating, erasure, withdrawal of consent where consent applies, and grievance handling. Submit a request through the Data Rights Request form or contact contact@ifranchise.in. Identity and request authority may need to be verified before any personal data is disclosed, changed or erased. The website does not automatically expose stored personal data.

sections.heading: Withdrawing consent
body: REQUIRES LEGAL REVIEW. Analytics consent can be rejected or withdrawn through the website privacy choices. For a previously submitted form, use the Data Rights Request form or the contact details below and identify the form or enquiry involved. Withdrawal does not itself determine whether information must be retained for another confirmed legal requirement; that assessment requires an internal verified process.

sections.heading: Children
body: REQUIRES LEGAL REVIEW. The website and franchise investment services are presented for adults, and the Terms state an age threshold of 18. The forms do not currently perform age or parental-authority verification. The business and counsel must confirm whether any child-data processing is possible and what prevention or verifiable-consent controls are required.

sections.heading: Changes to this notice
body: REQUIRES LEGAL REVIEW. This notice should be versioned when processing or legal requirements change. Material changes affecting consent should be presented for a fresh choice where required. A legal effective date must be approved rather than inferred solely from the website deployment date.

migrationNote: Original source draft. Update implementation-specific terms for CRM migration and retain draft status pending business/legal approval; do not publish outdated Google Sheets/Resend claims.

title: Licenses & Attribution

sections.heading: Overview
body: This Licenses page documents the software components, content rights, third-party integrations, and intellectual property frameworks that underpin the iFranchise platform. We are committed to transparency regarding the tools and technologies we use, and to honoring the licensing obligations associated with each.

sections.heading: Open Source Software
body: The iFranchise platform is built using open-source software components including React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and various npm ecosystem packages. Each component is used in accordance with its respective license - including MIT, Apache 2.0, and BSD variants. A full dependency manifest is maintained in our technical documentation and is available upon request.

sections.heading: Proprietary Platform Software
body: All custom software, algorithms, data models, and platform logic developed by iFranchise are proprietary and protected under applicable copyright and trade secret law. Unauthorized reproduction, reverse engineering, decompilation, or distribution of any proprietary component is strictly prohibited.

sections.heading: Franchise Brand Content
body: Franchise brand names, logos, trademarks, promotional materials, and business descriptions displayed on the iFranchise marketplace remain the exclusive intellectual property of their respective brand owners. iFranchise operates as a marketplace facilitator and does not claim ownership of any brand-specific content. All brand content is displayed under license or with explicit permission from the respective brand.

sections.heading: Platform Content and Design
body: All original content created by iFranchise - including editorial copy, UI design elements, iconography, illustrations, and data compilations - is protected under Indian and international copyright law. Users are granted a limited, non-exclusive right to view and interact with this content solely for legitimate business evaluation purposes. Any reproduction, redistribution, or commercial use requires prior written consent.

sections.heading: Third-Party Service Integrations
body: iFranchise integrates with third-party services for payment processing, analytics, cloud infrastructure, communication, and mapping. These integrations are governed by the respective service providers' terms of service and licensing agreements. iFranchise does not sublicense third-party services to users beyond what is necessary for platform functionality.

sections.heading: API Access and Usage
body: Access to any iFranchise API endpoints is subject to a separate API license agreement. Unauthorized access to, scraping of, or automated querying of platform APIs without a valid license is prohibited. Approved API partners must comply with rate limits, data handling requirements, and usage restrictions defined in their individual agreements.

sections.heading: User-Submitted Content
body: Content submitted by users - including franchise enquiry forms, profile information, reviews, and communications - remains the intellectual property of the submitting party. By submitting content to iFranchise, users grant us a worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to store, process, display, and use that content solely for the purpose of delivering platform services.

sections.heading: Trademarks
body: The iFranchise name, wordmark, logo, and associated brand identifiers are registered or common-law trademarks of iFranchise. Unauthorized use of these marks in any commercial context - including in domain names, advertising, or product names - is prohibited without explicit written authorization from iFranchise.

sections.heading: Data and Analytics
body: Aggregated, anonymized platform data and market insights generated by iFranchise are proprietary. This data may be used internally for product improvement, shared with franchise brand partners in aggregate form, or published as market research. Individual user data is never sold or shared in identifiable form without consent.

sections.heading: Geographic and Regulatory Compliance
body: iFranchise services are designed primarily for the Indian market and comply with applicable Indian regulatory frameworks including the Information Technology Act, 2000, and relevant data protection guidelines. Users accessing the platform from outside India are responsible for ensuring compliance with their local laws and regulations.

Material changes will be communicated through the platform. For licensing inquiries or to request attribution details, contact contact@ifranchise.in.
